content.title: No. 11 seed VCU overcomes 19-point deficit to upset No. 6 seed Tar Heels
content.text: GREENVILLE, S.C. (WBTV) - No. 11 seed Virginia Commonwealth University (VCU) upset one of the blue bloods in college basketball on Thursday night in the first round of the Men’s NCAA Basketball Tournament.The No. 11 seed VCU Rams upset the No. 6 seed North Carolina Tar Heels 82-78 in overtime in the first round on Thursday, March 19. The Tar Heels were without star Caleb Wilson, who was ruled out for the remainder of the season with a broken thumb.The Tar Heels led the Rams by 11, 39-28, at halftime. North Carolina quickly extended the lead to 19 points within the first five minutes of the second half. Read --> Top-ranked Duke survives first round scare against No. 16 SienaThe Tar Heels were up by 14 points with 7:11 left to play after a Jarin Stevenson three-pointer made it 70-56.The Rams went on a run to cut the lead down to two with just 3:05 left to play after a Terrence Hill Jr. layup made it 74-70.Hill later tied the game at 75-75 with 11 seconds to go on a layup, sending the game to overtime.Hill finished the game with 34 points and was 7-for-10 from beyond the arc. In overtime, it was all Rams as they outscored the Tar Heels 7-3. VCU’s Nyk Lewis got the scoring going on a layup to make it 77-75. Seth Trimble tied the game at 77-77 after a pair of free throws.Trimble gave North Carolina the lead with 35 seconds left to play after splitting a pair of free throws to make it 78-77. Hill gave the Rams the lead on a 3‑pointer to make it 80-78.With 4 seconds left to play, Henri Veesaar missed a pair of game-tying free throws. The 19-point lead was the biggest blown lead in the last 15 years. Copyright 2026 WBTV. All rights reserved.
